user.title: Yealink phone profile
user.description: Create one profile per phone or room. The profile ID becomes part of the URL, for example /api/yealink_xml/bedroom?view=menu. Select the entities this phone may access; use the entity selector's reorder controls to set their display order. Each profile has separate HTTP Basic credentials. Tap behavior controls whether selecting an item runs a default action or opens controls. After each action you can return to the main menu or remain on that entity. After an action, the phone waits up to the configured time for the entity to report its new state; it returns sooner if the state updates quickly. Home Assistant will suggest its configured internal URL or a discovered local address for the base URL when available; verify that your phone can reach it. Optional phone-control settings create buttons that send actions to the Yealink phone.

data_description.base_url: Home Assistant suggests its configured internal URL or a local address when available. Use an address reachable by the phone; Docker, VLAN, VPN, and multi-interface setups may need an override.
data_description.phone_url: For example: http://192.0.2.115. Leave blank to disable phone-control buttons. Plain HTTP sends the Basic Auth credentials without encryption; use a trusted LAN or HTTPS with a valid certificate.
data_description.phone_username: This is the phone web interface login, separate from the XML Browser credentials above.
data_description.phone_password: This is the phone web interface password. Home Assistant stores it in the config entry so it can authenticate each request; the value is not displayed again.
data_description.phone_verify_ssl: Leave enabled for trusted certificates. Disable only for an untrusted or factory certificate on a trusted local network; this skips HTTPS identity verification.
data_description.phone_actions: DND on/off are selected by default. DND must be enabled on the phone (features.dnd.allow=1). Also allow requests from Home Assistant under Features > Remote Control > Action URI Allow IP List. Also configure Features > Remote Control > Push XML Server IP Address to receive pushed notifications.

init.title: Yealink phone profile options
init.description: This profile's URL slug cannot be changed, so its phone URL stays stable. Rename the menu title, select/assign entities, and reorder them with the entity selector. Each profile only exposes the selected entities. To rotate HTTP Basic credentials, enter both new values; leave both blank to keep the current credentials. Tap behavior controls whether selecting an entity runs an action or opens its controls. After an action, you can return to the main phone menu or stay on the entity controls screen. In direct-action modes, a separate Controls row provides access to advanced actions such as brightness, volume, and media transport. State refresh wait is a maximum: the response returns as soon as Home Assistant reports a state or attribute change, or when the timeout expires. Phone control uses a separate phone web-interface login. Clear the phone URL to disable its action buttons. The saved phone password is reused when its field is left blank.

push_notification.name: Push notification
push_notification.description: Show a message on a Yealink phone, optionally with a beep or ringtone. Configure the phone to trust Home Assistant as its Push XML server first.

phone.name: Phone
phone.description: Select the configured Yealink phone to notify.

message.name: Message
message.description: The text to display on the phone.

title.name: Title
title.description: A short heading shown above the message.

beep.name: Beep
beep.description: Play a short notification tone when displaying the message.

ring.name: Play ringtone
ring.description: Play Ring1.wav with the message; the phone must have a usable ringer volume.

timeout.name: Screen timeout
timeout.description: Seconds before the phone leaves the notification screen (5–120).
